articles.title: GS House / Studio FP02
english: The GS House, completed in 2024, is nestled in the lush surroundings of Goiânia, Brazil. This residence was designed to establish a direct connection with the landscape, making it an integral part of its environment. The architectural approach emphasizes harmony between nature and living spaces, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for its inhabitants.

Covering an area of approximately 2,400 square meters, the house is situated in a gated community that provides not only privacy but also a sense of safety. The layout of the home is thoughtfully arranged to take advantage of natural light and views, promoting a seamless flow between indoors and outdoors. The design aims to create a tranquil retreat while maintaining a modern aesthetic.

The use of local materials in the construction of the GS House highlights the project's commitment to sustainability and environmental responsibility. This approach not only respects the surrounding nature but also supports the local economy by utilizing regional resources. Overall, the GS House serves as an exemplary model of thoughtful architecture that responds to its site.
chinese: GS住宅於2024年完成，坐落在巴西歌雅尼亞的郁郁蔥蔥環境中。這座住宅的設計旨在與周圍景觀建立直接的聯繫，使其成為環境不可或缺的一部分。建筑设计強調自然與居住空間之間的和諧，最終提升居民的生活質量。
這座房子佔地約2400平方米，位於一個提供隱私與安全感的封閉社區內。住宅的佈局經過深思熟慮，旨在充分利用自然光和景觀，促進室內與室外之間的無縫流動。設計旨在創造一個寧靜的避風港，同時保持現代美學。
GS住宅採用了當地材料，突顯了該項目對可持續性和環境責任的承諾。這一做法不僅尊重周圍自然，也通過利用本地資源來支持當地經濟。總的來說，GS住宅是對其場地反應的深思熟慮建築的典範。

articles.title: AtkinsRéalis to partner with Nvidia on nuclear-powered data centre design
english: AtkinsRéalis, a Canadian engineering firm, has partnered with Nvidia to design nuclear-powered data centres. This collaboration aims to create energy solutions for hyperscale centres that would otherwise stress traditional power grids. According to Sam Stephens, the digital head at AtkinsRéalis Nuclear, integrating nuclear power fundamentally alters the design and layout of AI campuses compared to conventional data centres.

The proposed designs for these nuclear-powered data centres will have capacities between 740MWe and 1000MWe, similar to small nuclear reactors. Nvidia’s proprietary technologies will facilitate an efficient planning process, potentially benefiting both the AI centres and local power grids. Stephens emphasized that the connection of a nuclear power plant to the grid could provide essential services to local communities.

The integration of nuclear power is expected to expand the footprint of each project while simultaneously reducing carbon emissions compared to existing data centre models. Co-locating AI data centres with nuclear plants allows for a more efficient and sustainable infrastructure model, where power generation, cooling systems, and grid connectivity are designed collaboratively. This innovation is anticipated to accelerate the commissioning of new projects as operators seek sustainable power supplies.
chinese: 加拿大工程公司AtkinsRéalis與科技公司Nvidia合作設計核能數據中心。這一合作旨在為超大規模數據中心創建能量解決方案，避免對傳統電網造成壓力。AtkinsRéalis核能部門的數字負責人Sam Stephens指出，整合核能會根本改變AI校園的設計與佈局，與傳統數據中心相比迥然不同。
這些核能數據中心的預計設計容量將介於740MWe到1000MWe之間，類似於小型核反應堆。Nvidia的專有技術將促進高效的規劃過程，可能惠及AI中心及當地電網。Stephens強調，核電廠與電網的連接可為當地社區提供基本服務。
核能的整合預期將擴大每個項目的建築面積，同時相較於現有的數據中心模型減少碳排放。將AI數據中心與核電廠共同設置，能夠實現更高效和可持續的基礎設施模型，發電、冷卻系統和電網聯接可共同設計。此創新預計將加速新項目的啟用，因為運營商尋求可持續的電力供應。

articles.title: safdie architects plans cherokee heritage center as a cluster of rammed earth blocks
english: The Cherokee Heritage Center, designed by Safdie Architects, is a thoughtful integration of architecture and landscape. The project features a series of rammed earth buildings shaped into low, faceted forms that harmonize with the surrounding wooded site. These buildings are organized to create a sense of continuity, inviting visitors to explore paths that weave through planted clearings and shallow water.

The use of rammed earth as the primary material gives the structure a unique texture that transitions from sandy beige to ochre, grounding it visually and physically in the environment. The varying roof shapes, from sharp peaks to gentle curves, create a dynamic silhouette that interacts with sunlight and the topography of the site. The design encourages natural light to permeate the interiors, enhancing the spatial experience.

Bridges and walkways connect the various buildings while maintaining a seamless flow between the indoor and outdoor environments. Outdoor spaces are incorporated as extensions of the architecture, blurring boundaries and promoting interaction with nature. Public areas, like the café, are strategically placed to offer views of the landscape, enhancing the visitors' experience.
chinese: 切羅基文化中心由薩夫迪建築師設計，巧妙地融合了建築與景觀。該項目展示了一系列的夯土建築，形狀為低矮的多面體，與周圍樹林景觀和諧統一。這些建築以連貫的方式組織，邀請遊客探索穿過綠植清理和淺水域的小路。
夯土作為主要材料使得結構具有獨特的質感，顏色從沙色過渡到赭色，視覺上和物理上扎根於環境中。不同的屋頂形狀，從尖銳的山峰到柔和的曲線，形成動態的輪廓，與陽光和地形互動。這種設計鼓勵自然光滲透到室內，增強空間體驗。
橋樑和步道連接著各個建築，同時保持室內外環境之間的無縫流動。戶外空間作為建築的延伸被融入，模糊了界限，促進了與自然的互動。公共區域，如咖啡廳， strategically 被放置以提供景觀視野，增強訪客的體驗。
